newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Seven killed in faction fighting in Mogadishu.
newsitem.headline: Seven killed in faction fighting in Mogadishu.

text.p: At least seven people were killed and 13 wounded in a clash on Tuesday between supporters of Somali faction leader Hussein Aideed and rival forces, doctors said.

The doctors at Hassan Jiis hospital and another hospital in southern Mogadishu said the seven dead and 13 wounded were brought in following the 30-minute clash between Hussein's militiamen and rival gunmen loyal to Osman Hassan Ali Atto.
Some witnesses said Aideed's forces attacked a base of Osman Atto's militia near south Mogadishu's Benadir hospital and both sides fought with mortars, machineguns and anti-aircraft batteries.
Forces under Aideed and Osman Atto have battled repeatedly despite Somali factions -- including both of them -- agreeing in Nairobi last month to end hostilities and remove roadblocks.

South Mogadishu has been hit since September by a string of assassinations, attacks and counter-attacks which Somali experts say are part of a vendetta between groups over the death of Hussein Aideed's father, Mohamed Farah Aideed, in early August.
Since last month supporters of Aideed have killed more than 10 people who backed Atto, a rival south Mogadishu faction leader whose forces are widely blamed for killing Mohamed Farah Aideed.

Hussein Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. marine, was elected to succeed his father as president of Somalia by supporters in August and heads a south Mogadishu-based government rejected by other leaders in Somalia as illegal.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow by rebels of late dictator president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
